hints.tiktokTokenRejected: TikTok is rejecting the Access Token itself. App ID and App Secret are NOT the cause — TikTok validates the token first, so this error appears whether or not those two are correct. Check: (1) you pasted the Access Token, not the auth_code from the redirect URL — an auth_code has to be exchanged at /oauth2/access_token/ first; (2) the token is for the TikTok Marketing API (business-api.tiktok.com), not TikTok Shop or Login Kit; (3) the app is not in Sandbox mode while you query live data; (4) the token has not been revoked or expired.
hints.tiktokTokenEmpty: The Access Token is empty. Enter one and test the connection again.
hints.tiktokAppCredentials: The Access Token works, but the App ID / App Secret were rejected — usually because the token was issued for a different app. Data endpoints only need the token, so they will work; advertiser-account discovery stays unavailable until the App ID/Secret match the app that issued the token.
hints.tiktokNoAdvertiser: The token is valid but no advertiser account has authorised this app. Authorise an advertiser account for the app in TikTok Ads Manager, then test again.
hints.tiktokRateLimited: TikTok is rate-limiting these calls (too many requests in a short time, per app or per ad account). This is not a permission or token problem — wait a minute and try again.
hints.tiktokPermission: The token is valid but the app lacks the scope for this endpoint. Review the app permissions in the Developer Portal and issue a new token.
hints.tiktokNeedsProbe: Nothing to verify the token against. Provide App ID + App Secret, or a default Advertiser ID, so a request can be made.
hints.tiktokUnknown: TikTok returned an error that is not in the known list. Read the exact wording below and check the provider documentation.
hints.sapoUnauthorized: Sapo rejected the credentials. Check that the Access Token is still valid, or that the API key/secret pair is correct and the private app is still enabled.
hints.sapoNotFound: The store domain is wrong. Use store.mysapo.net (Sapo Web) or store.mysapogo.com (Sapo POS/Omni), not a custom domain pointed at the shop.
hints.sapoMissingCredentials: Credentials are missing. Provide an Access Token, or both the API Key and API Secret.
hints.sapoShopForbidden: Connected. This private app has not been granted access to store information, so the store name, currency and timezone will not show. To get them, open this private app under Sapo → Apps and grant that permission.
hints.sapoNoPermission: Sapo accepted the API key/secret, but the private app has no permission to read orders, products or customers. Open this private app under Sapo → Apps, enable the permissions you need, then test again.
hints.tiktokBothWrong: TikTok rejected both the App ID/Secret and the Access Token. Re-copy the App ID and Secret from the Developer Portal, then edit this connection: enter the new pair and paste a fresh auth_code into the auth_code field — the old token almost certainly belongs to a different app.
hints.tiktokExchangeOk: The auth_code was exchanged for an Access Token and stored (encrypted). The code itself is not kept, since it is single-use.
hints.tiktokExchangeFailed: TikTok would not exchange this auth_code. It is SINGLE-USE and expires quickly — authorise the app again for a fresh code and save straight away.
hints.tiktokExchangeNeedsApp: App ID and App Secret are needed to exchange an auth_code. Fill both in and save again.
hints.tiktokNeedsCodeOrToken: Fill in ONE of two things: the auth_code from the URL TikTok redirects to after you authorise the app (…/callback/?auth_code=XXXX), or an Access Token if you already have one.
hints.tiktokCodeAlreadyUsed: This auth_code has already been used, or it expired. Each code works exactly ONCE — authorise the app again in TikTok, copy the auth_code from the new redirect URL, and save straight away. If an earlier exchange already succeeded, the Access Token is on the connection and there is nothing to redo.
hints.permissionsAll: Every read-only endpoint that was tried is permitted. The "skipped" lines are writing endpoints, deliberately not called, or endpoints still missing a required parameter.
hints.permissionsPartial: Some endpoints were refused by the provider. Usually the app lacks the matching scope — review the app permissions in the Developer Portal and issue a new token.
hints.permissionsNone: No endpoint is permitted. That almost always means the credentials are wrong or the token was revoked — run "Diagnose each credential" first.

hub.customTitle: Call any endpoint the provider exposes
hub.customIntro: Neither TikTok nor Sapo publishes a machine-readable spec (checked), so a hand-written catalogue will always trail the real API. This sends straight to the path you type, using the connection credentials — no code change. The path is joined to the provider base URL and refused if it tries to leave it.
hub.customPathHelp: For example /app/info/ or /admin/locations.json. Absolute URLs are refused — the path is always joined to the connection base URL.
hub.customBodyHelp: Used for non-GET methods only. Must be valid JSON.
hub.customResultPathHelp: Optional. For example data.list (TikTok) or orders (Sapo) — fill it in to make the Records and Schema tabs work.
hub.customWriteWarning: This method can change data on the provider side
hub.customForbiddenWrite: Only Admins and above may send a writing method through a free-form path, because nothing has reviewed what that endpoint does.
hub.customBadPath: The path was refused. Only relative paths inside the provider base URL are accepted — no absolute URLs, no "..", no control characters, no %2f/%2e.
hub.customBadBody: The body is not valid JSON.
hub.unverifiedTitle: This endpoint was declared from its path, not read from the docs
hub.unverifiedBody: TikTok publishes no machine-readable spec, so the method and parameters here are inferred from the path name. The path is real; the parameter list is almost certainly incomplete. If TikTok reports a missing parameter, look it up and add it to the Body (JSON) field, or use the free-form request tab. It cannot be saved as a dataset because the field that identifies a record has not been established.

systemUpdate.title: System update
systemUpdate.subtitle: Ship a new version from the development machine to the server. The server applies it only once an Administrator types the right confirmation code.
systemUpdate.notConfiguredTitle: This machine is not set up for updates
systemUpdate.notConfiguredHint: On the development machine: add UPDATE_SERVER_URL (the server address) and UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY (the key the server printed at install) to .env.local, then restart. On the server, the installer turns it on.
systemUpdate.sendTitle: Send an update to the server
systemUpdate.sendHint: Packs the code on this machine — no data, dependencies or .env files — signs it with the update key and sends it to {server}. The server applies it only once it is confirmed with the code.
systemUpdate.versionLoading: Asking the server for its current version…
systemUpdate.versionServerUnknown: Could not get the server’s version
systemUpdate.versionHint: Bumped from the current version — change it if you like.
systemUpdate.versionNotHigher: This version is not above the one the server runs ({version}). It can still be sent, but the update history gets harder to follow.
systemUpdate.codeHint: Open System update on {server} and type this code before {time}. It works once.

senderProblem.key: UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY is missing from .env.local (or too short).
senderProblem.url: UPDATE_SERVER_URL is not valid — it needs an https:// address.

sendError.forbidden: Only an Administrator can send updates.
sendError.notConfigured: This machine has no UPDATE_SERVER_URL and UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY.
sendError.version: The version is not valid — use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. 1.2.3.
sendError.signature: The server refused the signature — check that UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY is exactly the same on both machines.
sendError.stale: The server refused it: the two machines’ clocks are more than 5 minutes apart.
sendError.busy: The server is applying another update, or has just received too many. Try again in a few minutes.
sendError.notReceiver: The server does not accept updates (UPDATE_RECEIVER).
sendError.server: The server answered with an error ({detail}).

systemUpdate.pendingNone: No update is waiting. Send one from this page on the development machine.
systemUpdate.codeInputHint: Shown on the development machine after sending, as XXXX-XXXX.

confirmError.notReceiver: This server does not accept updates.
confirmError.problem: This server cannot update itself yet — see the warnings above.
confirmError.notFound: This update is no longer here.
confirmError.expired: The update has expired. Send it again from the development machine.
confirmError.locked: Too many wrong codes, so the update was discarded. Send it again from the development machine.

problem.key: The server has no UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY (or it is too short).
problem.layout: The app does not run in the installer’s layout (releases / current / shared), so it cannot update itself.
problem.embedded: The server runs the embedded database, which cannot be updated while the app runs. Use PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL).

systemUpdate.restarting: The server is restarting — the page reconnects by itself when it is back.

state.failed: The update failed. The previous version keeps running as before.
state.rolled-back: The new version did not start, so the previous one was put back.

systemUpdate.backupAt: Database backup taken before the update: {file}
